question: Under the cheapest law of the study of parts that meet again under which parts meet, with both of its rations, is there a pattern the growth makes that, on meeting a second pattern, leaves two of the second: two parts the same as it, two renamings of its knots among the made knots, or two usable loose made distinctions tied to one of its places; for which class of second patterns; and how much of any case is the supplied choice of which shared distinction a birth takes, the start's numbering, or the start itself?
inputs: The starts, base laws, taking rules, rules for which distinction a birth takes, renamings, take lists, record structures and bounds named in the pre-registration and its data files; this study's definitions and claim; the definitions of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001 and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the engine of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001A, unchanged, as the growth code and as the gate's reference.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration and the owner's arm disclose; any change to the fold study's engine; any rule added so that something is copied.
primary_observable: For every registered run: the three readings of 'two of it' by descent at every round read; the conditions of a copier (made by the first pattern, with the second replaced, not the first pattern's own, surviving every renaming registered for the design, for the whole class); the three verdicts (who made the two, what fixed the takes, where the first pattern and the shared distinction that joins the two come from); the readings of the owner's arm; the fresh count of every birth; every tie class containing a made distinction; the knot test of every knot under the run's own knot law.
comparators_or_controls: The base laws with no taking rule; the second pattern barred; the first pattern barred; the first pattern alone; the second pattern replaced by each other member of its class; the control with the second pattern the same as the first; the controls of the readings (the record's counts, a part and knots placed by hand); every choice of take as a control with registered take lists; the swaps of run 5; the rations outside the registered ones in run O.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 8 GB on one process; anything longer through the shared runner with a row in the long-running index. Bounds: 6 rounds (8 for one reading on a case); a run stops after the first round past 500 knots; the fold study's guard.
first_executable_signal: The gate P0 and the controls of the readings P14; then the fresh count of every birth (P1) and the registered take lists replayed (P8a).
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column; checks, replications and reported readings are marked as such.
stop_rule: Stop when, for each reading and each knot law, there is a first pattern with the class for which it is a copier and its three verdicts, or a reason no made pattern can under that law, or, where neither is reached, the bounded report named in the pre-registration; and every registered run has been made and every prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of rules added by hand on starts built by hand, to six rounds. A failure of every registered claim is about one first pattern, four stated rules and the registered classes; it is no reason that no made pattern can leave two of what it meets. The owner's idea that copying is a pattern and not a law (assumption A244) and his inkling that no copier can be general (A248) are recorded as his and are not evidence. His later idea, to use up the second pattern and leave two, is not tested here. No claim about living things, minds, physics or time.
